The lowest common ancestor of Ramipril and Benazepril is identified as an Organic Heterobicyclic Compound, which is a common structural feature among Ace Inhibitors. This structural similarity may explain the binding affinity of Benazepril to Ace, suggesting a possible mechanism by which Ramipril influences Ace through its interaction with Benazepril. The evidence supports a plausible pathway where Ramipril's effects are indirectly linked to Ace via Benazepril, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
